problem: Model-free RL navigation is data-inefficient and generalizes poorly to new targets and scenes, while model-based methods suffer from model imperfection and over-regularized latent spaces that hurt cross-scene generalization.
motivation: Mapless target-driven visual navigation must generalize across targets and scenes with visual and structural discrepancies. Modeling forward dynamics (action-driven observation transition) with an expressive latent space should give data efficiency and better generality than reactive policies.
key_idea: Train a conditional variational model that imagines the next expected observation (NEO) given the current multi-view observation and the target view, with a mixture-of-posteriors prior conditioned on current observation and next best action, and predict the action from the generated NEO features.
insight: The ablations on AVD (Table 2, no stop) show both the generative NEO modeling (NoGen avg 34.8/21.7 vs full 47.7/25.5) and the mixture-of-posteriors prior (NoMoP 40.3/21.7) matter; multi-view input also helps (FrontView 37.1/15.6). t-SNE shows the MoP latent space is structured by action while the standard-normal prior is unstructured. Data-efficiency is also shown: with only 2 training scenes the method reaches 35.1 SR versus at most 26.1 for the baselines.
method: Variational inference module: ResNet-50 features of K-view current observation and target view (64x64) go through an MLP/FC stack to a 400-D Gaussian latent z (reparameterization trick)
Mixture-of-posteriors prior p(z|x,a): a Gaussian conditioned on the front-view observation and the ground-truth action, used only in training as the KL target

NEO generation module: two FC layers plus a 5-layer transposed-conv decoder generates the next front-view observation, supervised by the ground-truth next observation (L2 on features in the simplified version)
Action prediction module: 4-layer MLP over the decoder feature, current-observation feature and previous-action embedding predicts one of 7 discrete actions (cross-entropy)

Objective: alpha*reconstruction + beta*KL + gamma*classification with alpha=0.01, beta=0.0001, gamma=1; the ResNet and classifier are pretrained until about 70% action accuracy, then joint training with SGD
Testing: NEO is not actually generated; the target-conditioned latent feeds the action head; collision detection falls back to the next most probable action

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + MLP VAE (encoder/decoder) + MLP action classifier, trained with supervision
setting.training_data: Shortest-path (A*) ground-truth trajectories on grid-based scenes: AVD (8 training houses, ~616k samples) and AI2-THOR (20 training scenes per room category, separate model per category); 15 target views per training scene
setting.observation: K-view azimuth observations (6 views in AVD, 4 in AI2-THOR) of depth (default), RGB or RGB-D at 64x64, plus target view image
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward/back/left/right, rotate cw/ccw, stop, on a 0.25-0.5 m grid
setting.simulator: Active Vision Dataset (real-world grid-based scenes) and AI2-THOR
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth shortest-path actions only for training)

results: On unseen AVD scenes NeoNav (depth) reaches 47.7 SR / 25.5 SPL without stop and 19.9 / 5.9 with stop, beating TD-A3C (32.2 / 5.2 and 14.2 / 1.8), I2A and Gated-LSTM-A3C by more than 5% SR. On AI2-THOR it averages 16.7 SR versus 11.7 for TD-A3C, and in semantic-driven navigation it exceeds TD-Semantic (66.3 vs 53.6 average SR).
limitations: Requires dense supervised ground-truth paths and is not integrated with RL; absolute success rates in the strict stop setting and on reversed tasks remain low (19.9%, 32.4%)
Struggles with cramped spaces, corners, transparent or texture-less scenes (bathrooms), and long-range unseen targets
Evaluated only on grid-based discrete scenes in simulation or captured datasets, with custom protocols and no real robot
